text: After a long time, in the third year, the word of the LORD came to Elijah: Go present yourself to Ahab; I will send rain on the land.
So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab, while the famine in Samaria was severe.
Ahab summoned Obadiah, his palace administrator, who deeply feared the LORD.
When Jezebel was killing off the LORD's prophets, Obadiah had taken a hundred of them, hidden them in two caves in groups of fifty, and supplied them with food and water.
Ahab told Obadiah, Go through the land to every spring and valley; maybe we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive so we don't lose all our animals.
So they divided the land between them to cover it — Ahab went one way alone, and Obadiah went another way alone.
As Obadiah was walking along, Elijah met him; Obadiah recognized him, fell facedown, and said, Is that really you, my lord Elijah?
Elijah answered, Yes, it's me. Go tell your master, Elijah is here.
Obadiah said, What have I done wrong that you would hand your servant over to Ahab to be killed?

As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my master has not sent someone searching for you; whenever a kingdom or nation claimed you weren't there, he made them swear they hadn't found you.
And now you tell me to go tell my master, Elijah is here?

As soon as I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD may carry you off to who knows where, and when I tell Ahab and he can't find you, he will kill me — even though I, your servant, have feared the LORD since my youth.
Wasn't my lord told what I did when Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets — how I hid a hundred of them in two caves, fifty at a time, and supplied them with food and water?
And now you tell me to go tell my master, Elijah is here? He will kill me!
Elijah said, As surely as the LORD Almighty lives, whom I serve, I will present myself to Ahab today.
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw him, he said, Is that you, you troubler of Israel?
Elijah replied, I have not troubled Israel; you and your father's family have, by abandoning the LORD's commands and following the Baals.
Now summon all Israel to meet me at Mount Carmel, along with the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table.
So Ahab sent word throughout Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.
Elijah went before the people and said, How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; if Baal is God, follow him. But the people said nothing.
Elijah said, I am the only prophet of the LORD left, while Baal has 450 prophets.
Give us two bulls; let them choose one, cut it up, and place it on wood without setting fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and place it on wood without fire.
Then you call on your god's name, and I will call on the LORD's name; the god who answers with fire — he is God. All the people agreed this was a good plan.
Elijah told the prophets of Baal, Choose one bull and prepare it first, since there are many of you; call on your god's name, but don't light the fire.

So they took the bull given them and prepared it, and they called on Baal's name from morning until noon, shouting, Baal, answer us! But there was no sound, no answer; they danced around the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah began mocking them: Shout louder! Surely he's a god — maybe he's deep in thought, or busy, or traveling; perhaps he's sleeping and must be woken up.
So they shouted louder and cut themselves with swords and spears, as was their custom, until blood flowed.
Midday passed, and they kept up their frantic prophesying until the time of the evening offering, but there was no sound, no answer, no response at all.
Then Elijah told all the people, Come near to me, and they gathered around him; he repaired the LORD's altar, which had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes descended from Jacob, whom the LORD had named Israel.
With the stones he rebuilt the altar in the LORD's name and dug a trench around it wide enough to hold about two seahs of seed.
He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, laid it on the wood, and said, Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the offering and the wood.
Do it again, he said, and they did; do it a third time, he said, and they did that too.
The water flowed all around the altar, and he even filled the trench with it.

At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet stepped forward and prayed: LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things at your command.
Answer me, LORD, answer me, so this people will know that you, LORD, are God, and that you are turning their hearts back to you.
Then the fire of the LORD fell and burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench.
When all the people saw it, they fell facedown and cried out, The LORD, he is God! The LORD, he is God!
Elijah told them, Seize the prophets of Baal; don't let a single one escape. They seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley and had them killed there.
Elijah said to Ahab, Go, eat and drink, for I hear the sound of a heavy rain coming.
So Ahab went to eat and drink, while Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.
He told his servant, Go and look toward the sea. The servant went, looked, and said, There's nothing there. Seven times Elijah told him to go back and look.
On the seventh time the servant said, A cloud as small as a man's hand is rising from the sea. Elijah said, Go tell Ahab, Hitch up your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.
Meanwhile the sky grew black with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall; Ahab rode off toward Jezreel.
The power of the LORD came on Elijah; he tucked his cloak into his belt and outran Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
